messages:
nisha_cs: Quick heads-up: OrbitLab onboarding stuck. They report intermittent 403s during token exchange, then a large burst of requests that trigger 429s on our edge. Customer uses python-sdk v1.2.0 and an enterprise API gateway that injects a tracking cookie.
nisha_cs: Carlos pasted this from their infra: "gateway rewrites Cookie header and appends tracking=base64(json) ~ 420 bytes; when combined with our Authorization header it exceeds gateway allowed header size -> gateway returns 403. Client retries immediatey and we see many short lived preflight requests."
carlos_orbitlab: Yep, our gateway team added extra cookie bits for analytics. We didn't expect it to interact with your handshake.
tom_eng: Thanks. Two quick hypotheses: 1) Header size overflow causing gateway to drop or rewrite Authorization -> 403. 2) SDK retry policy without jitter causing request stampede -> 429 later.
li_sre: We also see in our access logs a sudden spike in connection attempts from their IPs with many different TLS sessions (cold start fanout). That matches their lambda-based workers.
rachel_support: OrbitLab is on a tight POC timeline. What can we recommend that is low friction?
tom_eng: Low-friction fixes: A) Ask gateway team to exclude our /v1/auth path from cookie injection (route-level cookie strip). B) Short-term: send the long analytics object as a POST body to an internal analytics endpoint instead of a cookie. C) Patch client to move any non-required auth metadata into request body for the handshake.
carlos_orbitlab: We can try route-level cookie strip. Would you prefer we also change the python-sdk behavior?
tom_eng: Yes, please. Recommend upgrading to python-sdk v1.2.3 which has two changes: backoff jitter on initial 5 auth attempts, and a opt-in preflight coalescing feature for serverless cold starts. If they can't upgrade immediately, provide a tiny wrapper: 
```
# quick patch wrapper
import time, random

def auth_with_backoff(auth_fn, attempts=5):
    for i in range(attempts):
        try:
            return auth_fn()
        except Exception as e:
            sleep_ms = (2**i * 100) + random.randint(0,150)
            time.sleep(sleep_ms/1000.0)
    raise RuntimeError('auth failed')
```

li_sre: Also recommended: set client short-lived connection reuse (keepalive) so cold starts reuse sockets and reduce TLS overhead.
rachel_support: OrbitLab says they deploy many tiny workers. Any docs we can point them to for gateway config?
li_sre: Point them to our onboarding checklist page under "proxy & gateway quirks". It already mentions header-size limits but not analytics cookie interactions. I'll add a note.
devex_bot: TODO added: docs/onboarding/proxy-cookie-interactions.md :white_check_mark:
nisha_cs: Carlos, please try (1) route-level cookie strip for /v1/auth and (2) apply the auth wrapper or upgrade SDK. We'll monitor for 24h.
carlos_orbitlab: We're doing the route-strip now. Also scheduling an SDK upgrade for this afternoon.
tom_eng: One more telemetry ask: can we emit a metric when Authorization length > 300 bytes for first-call failures? That would help detect this class of problem early.
li_sre: +1, filing infra ticket to surface auth header length on first-failure traces.
nisha_cs: Thanks everyone. If orbitlab sees success we'll mark onboarding green; otherwise we'll reconvene. :thumbsup:
carlos_orbitlab: Quick update 30m later: route strip fixed the 403s. After SDK upgrade and backoff patch, we saw the retry bursts collapse and no 429s in the last hour. Appreciate the quick help.
